Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · v0.8.0

The spell lingers.
The game keeps moving.

30+ Region and aura configurations. 100+ creature-effect recipes. This release brings supported Player’s Handbook spells and Monster Manual features into adjustable libraries—so the next save, escape attempt, or damage prompt can arrive without someone remembering to ask for it.

Use the built-in defaults, tailor them to your table, or turn them off. The books provide the content; you choose how much the module handles.

Built-in automation libraries

Ready to run.
Ready to make your own.

  • Your existing Region automations, now built in. The previous world-based Region setup has been migrated into a standard library of module defaults. Existing saved configurations are preserved as local overrides, so your table’s adjustments stay in control. Edit or modify a recipe, disable it, restore its default, or add a new Region automation of your own.
  • Find the automation you need. Search built-in creature triggers and Region recipes, then view or edit their settings.
  • Keep your table’s rules. Override defaults, add custom entries, restore a recipe, or disable it outright. Module updates preserve your local overrides.
  • Built around the books you own. Defaults use supported native Player’s Handbook and Monster Manual activities and effects. The books remain separate purchases; their content is not bundled.
Monster Manual effects

Let the monsters
follow through.

  • Remember lingering conditions. Supported poison, fear, paralysis, charm, incapacitation, and unconsciousness effects prompt repeat saves and clear on success after the dice finish.
  • Offer an escape. Optional action prompts use the originating monster’s escape DC and skill choices. The person clicking handles the skill choice and roll.
  • Make ongoing damage count. Attachments, grapples, smothering, whirlwind, and swallowing trigger on the correct creature’s turn. Swallow replaces the same monster’s grapple and avoids double-dipping into its external aura.
  • Bring the aura to the fight. Supported monster auras start with combat and stay hidden from players by default. Eligible fear and Stench saves track their supported immunity rules.
  • Treat the wound. Infernal wounds support recurring HP loss, Apply/Undo, Medicine treatment, and closure when a spell restores HP.
Spell areas & lingering magic

From first contact
to the final save.

  • More areas, less repetition. Expanded spell Regions cover damage areas, walls, clouds, and emanations, with configured entry, movement, and turn triggers.
  • Keep summons connected. Flaming Sphere gains a token-attached area. Guardian of Faith tracks damage against its pool and removes its guardian and area when exhausted.
  • Remember what happens later. Supported creature effects handle recurring damage and healing, delayed damage, repeat saves, optional action escapes, and Blink.
  • Keep placement separate from persistence. Targeting-only areas can clear while creature effects remain. Movement-only damage waits until a creature actually moves through the area.
Smite, Cleave & spellbooks

More choices.
Fewer extra steps.

  • Use the Smite you prepared. Choose supported prepared Smite spells in weapon damage options. Their initial damage joins the weapon roll; save-based Smites create the necessary follow-up save card.
  • Cleave from the hit. A qualifying attack card offers a separate Cleave attack against a different target, with the correct ability-modifier adjustment and eligible weapon/feature bonuses.
  • Keep your spell list ready. Clerics, Druids, and other supported full-list preparation casters can load missing available spells from Add Spell, ready to prepare.
  • Keep reactions and corrections usable. Improved save/effect handling and target displays keep results and recorded recipients connected through the workflow.
Control & cleanup

Automate the routine.
Keep the decisions.

  • Set the level of assistance. Automatic damage, healing, and effect application remain independent choices. Applying damage or effects locks relevant corrections until Undo reopens them.
  • Clean up after combat. Clear inactive applied effects automatically or from the actor window menu, preserving disabled class/item features and active effects.
  • Keep play flowing. Turn-processing improvements, duplicate-card protection, concentration replacement fixes, and animation-aware cleanup reduce interruptions.
  • Leave special interactions at the table. Shared damage between creatures and life-stealing effects that reduce maximum HP or heal another creature remain manual. The GM also handles movement, range, capacity, counters, and effects with multiple stages or choices.
Updating to v0.8.0

A fresh start
for your next encounter.

Restart Foundry after updating, then reload GM and player clients. Apply fresh effects or recast areas to use changed triggers. Existing local overrides remain in control. Tested with Foundry VTT v14 and D&D5e 6.0.6.
